# Week 20 Appendix: A Week of High Pressure, No Movement

*Executive expansion collided with judicial resistance across immigration, spending, and information control, leaving the clock exactly where it stood.*

![Header image](image_wide_week20_appendix.png)

This was a high-pressure week defined by executive aggrandizement, coercive immigration enforcement, politicization of state capacity, and widening fusion between public power and private loyalty networks. The strongest structural pressures came from repeated efforts to bypass Congress on spending and workforce cuts, aggressive use of immigration machinery with weak due-process protections, retaliation or threatened retaliation against media, universities, and private actors, and a broad hollowing of administrative competence in public-health, weather, disaster, and veterans systems. Courts provided meaningful but uneven resistance: several judges blocked deportations, protected labor rights, and checked some executive actions, yet appellate and Supreme Court interventions also enabled tariff enforcement, DOGE data access, and narrower discovery into executive conduct. The week also showed democratic decay operating through policy substance, not just rhetoric: budget and regulatory moves targeted welfare provision, scientific independence, public media, and civic inclusion, while patronage, donor influence, and personal feuds around government contracts underscored a governing style in which loyalty and leverage increasingly displace neutral administration.

1. The Department of Energy cut staff and eliminated regulations (2025-05-31) *[single source]*: The staffing cuts and deregulation reduced administrative capacity and shifted policy power away from professional oversight inside a major federal agency.
